title: 竹林清响 Zhulin Qingxiang
subtitle: Yuanming Yuan

model.line: On the block drawn on the Qing plan S01: position and frontage from the plan, heights and roof from the typology of its hall class, its form drawn by the hall kit. It will be updated as the research goes on.
rows: platform 0.54 m, eave 3.64 m, ridge 5.77 m above the ground
gable 硬山 or 悬山, rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile

by the hall kit: 5 bays, the middle widest, a porch front, steps on the front, 硬山 flush gable with a rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile, a painted beam under the eave. Drawn from the typology of its hall class, not from a picture of this hall (assumed, C).

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 勤政亲贤
evidence.excerpt_zh: 勤政親賢之東為飛雲軒東有閣為靜鑑其北為懐清芬又北為秀木佳䕃轉後為生秋庭靜鑑閣東為芳碧叢後為保合太和正殿三楹後為富春樓樓東為竹林清響（圓圓明園册）臣等謹按飛雲軒懐清芬秀木佳䕃生秋庭諸額皆御書保合太和殿壁恭懸御書聖訓四箴箴已載養心殿卷内不備録其西暖閣亦有勤政親賢額西暖閣内額曰叢雲曰養性北曰隨安室富春樓下額曰坐擁琳琅曰蔚然深秀曰無倦齋曰清風明月樓與竹林清響額皆御書
evidence.summary: East of 勤政親賢 stand 飛雲軒, the 靜鑑閣 pavilion, 懐清芬, 秀木佳䕃, 生秋庭 and 芳碧叢; then 保合太和殿 of three bays with 富春樓 and 竹林清響 behind. The note lists plaques, including a second 勤政親賢 plaque and a 隨安室 in the west warm room.

evidence.title: 竹林清响: 嘉庆元年 poem of the Jiaqing Emperor
evidence.date: 嘉庆元年 (1796), date from the compilation
evidence.locator: p.110 item (1), under 竹林清响
evidence.excerpt_zh: 万个筼筜罨翠深，七贤物外漫招寻。窗前清响凉飔送，日日平安报好音。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Jiaqing Emperor at 竹林清响, 1796, on the view. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 竹林清响: 嘉庆二年 poem of the Jiaqing Emperor
evidence.date: 嘉庆二年 (1797), date from the compilation
evidence.locator: p.110 item (2), under 竹林清响
evidence.excerpt_zh: 浮筠绕亭榭，渐觉碧云深。烟羃筼筜色，风吹箫管音。吟怀千亩迹，思入五弦琴。晤坐聆清响，七贤忆竹林。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Jiaqing Emperor at 竹林清响, 1797, on the view. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编: 竹林清响
evidence.locator: from p.110, under 正大光明
evidence.summary: 竹林清响: 2 dated items, 1796-1797, of which 2 poems (Jiaqing); recurring themes: the view. First dated 1796, last dated 1797.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
